item.title: AFG vs IND: Essential Guide to the 3rd ODI Showdown
item.description:
AFG vs IND: Essential Guide to the 3rd ODI Showdown

What if a so-called “dead rubber” was actually the most revealing match of the series? That is exactly the question hovering over the AFG vs IND third ODI in Chennai, where India can complete a clean sweep — and Afghanistan can finally land a punch on a side that has steamrolled them across two matches.

Quick Summary

  • India lead the three-match ODI series 2-0 after wins in Dharamsala and Lucknow.
  • The 3rd ODI is being played at the M. A. Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai on June 20, 2026.
  • Shubman Gill has scores of 84* and 154 so far; Gurnoor Brar has six wickets in two games.
  • Returning to the XI: Nitish Kumar Reddy, Prasidh Krishna, and Harshit Rana (back from a knee injury).
  • Afghanistan won the toss in the 3rd ODI and opted to bat first.

The matchup matters far beyond the scorecard. It is a live audition for India’s middle order ahead of a packed white-ball calendar, and a stress test for an Afghanistan side still searching for its first ODI win against a top-ranked opponent in this cycle.

item.title: IPL Standings 2026: Surprising Shake-Up at the Top
item.description:
Did you know Punjab Kings, a franchise that has never lifted the trophy, is the only unbeaten team six matches into IPL 2026? The IPL standings this season are rewriting expectations, and the defending champions are scrambling to catch up.

Quick Summary: Punjab Kings top the IPL 2026 points table with 11 points and a net run rate of +1.420. Royal Challengers Bengaluru moved to second after a five-wicket win over Gujarat Titans, powered by Virat Kohli’s 81. Sunrisers Hyderabad climbed into the top three after Match 31, while Mumbai Indians slipped to eighth.

item.title: Ayush Mhatre's Explosive IPL 2026 Fifty Sets Chepauk on Fire
item.description:
Ayush Mhatre’s Explosive IPL 2026 Fifty Sets Chepauk on Fire

An 18-year-old walking out to bat at the iconic M.A. Chidambaram Stadium, surviving a bizarre bat-gauge mishap, and then unleashing a boundary barrage that left Punjab Kings scrambling — that was Ayush Mhatre on April 3, 2026.

Key Takeaways

  • Mhatre scored a power-laden half-century for CSK against PBKS in Match No. 7 of IPL 2026
  • He joined an elite list alongside Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Prithvi Shaw as one of the youngest IPL fifty scorers
  • CSK were cruising at 101/1 after 10 overs, powered by Mhatre’s aggression
  • The innings came after a comical umpire error where the bat gauge was held upside down

From Bat-Gauge Drama to Boundary Blitz

Before Mhatre could even take his guard at No. 3, a bizarre incident unfolded at Chepauk. On-field umpire Abhijit Bhattacharya subjected Mhatre’s bat to a thickness test — and it failed. Mhatre signaled to the dugout for a replacement, but that bat failed too.
